evidence: src/application/catalogue-service.ts: CatalogueService(products: ProductRepository) exposes addProduct, listProducts, getProduct and restock, and delegates stock changes to Product.restock.

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService(orders, products, ids, clock) exposes placeOrder, transition, advance and cancel, and delegates to Order.advanceTo, Order.nextState, Order.cancel and Product.canReserve, reserve, release and consumeReserved.
Both services return ProductSnapshot or OrderSnapshot through toSnapshot(), so the output boundary is the same.
Minor duplication: private requireProduct(id) is identical in catalogue-service.ts and order-service.ts and throws NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`).
placeOrder checks every line with canReserve before calling reserve on any of them, which keeps the all-or-nothing reservation in one method.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files cover one concern: application use cases over the shop's domain model. CatalogueService handles product management and OrderService handles the order lifecycle. Both inject only domain ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator, Clock) and return snapshots (toSnapshot). Domain rules stay inside the domain objects: Product.canReserve, reserve, release, consumeReserved and restock, and Order.advanceTo, nextState and cancel. Neither service changes entity state directly, so the module's own abstractions are not bypassed. The one duplication is the private requireProduct helper, which appears identically in both services and throws NotFoundError(`Product ${id} not found`). This is a small lookup-or-throw convenience, not a business rule or invariant, so I treat it as a minor smell, not a failure. The empty-items check in placeOrder might repeat validation inside the Order constructor, but order.ts is not provided and the code comment says Order validates quantities and duplicate lines, not emptiness, so I cannot confirm duplication.
